summary.headline: John Cockerill India Q2 CY26 standalone revenue up 82% YoY to ~INR149 crore; consolidated INR299 crore (+18% YoY), order book ~INR4,500 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue rose 82% YoY to about INR149 crore and consolidated revenue reached about INR299 crore, up 18% YoY, but both fell sequentially as Q1 benefited from closing older projects. Management attributed weaker Q2 margins to upfront costs on newly started projects, organisation-building spend and one-time consolidation costs after the China, Germany and Belgium entities were brought under the listed company. Order wins of about INR1,200 crore in the quarter lifted the consolidated order book to about INR4,500 crore (standalone about INR2,200 crore). Management expects revenue and margins to build in H2 as new projects ramp, though it gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Expected marginally lower in next two quarters

segments.name: Standalone (India)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR149 crore, up 82% YoY; top customers Tata Steel and JSW. Order book ~INR2,200 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR299 crore, up 18% YoY; ArcelorMittal to be added to top customers after consolidation. Order book ~INR4,500 crore. Top five customers ~80% of revenue.

segments.name: Value-added services
segments.commentary: Service revenue in Q2 about one-third of Q1; management says lower because project progress was slower, not lack of orders, and services margins remain strong.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated INR8,000 crore top-line as the CY30 north-star, to come from organic growth (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions; several acquisitions under evaluation, no timeline given.
Management said consolidated revenue in H2 should improve significantly; did not expect to reach the ~INR2,000 crore CY25 pro-forma figure but 'should not be very far' if US is included.
Execution of new orders to ramp in Q3 and Q4 as engineering and procurement progress; impact on H2.
Employee cost expected to rise as manpower is added on the execution side; other expenses to be marginally lower than Q2 level in the next two quarters.
One-time transaction, forex and notional interest costs expected to stop from H2 after the parent agreed to a share-based payment instead of cash.
Further order wins expected before year-end across Asia, Europe, US and India; a JVD contract in Asia is in advanced discussion, targeted this year.
capex_capacity: Taloja Rolls Coating facility put into operation in June 2026; testing and trial orders underway, production initiation now.
Advanced Coating facility at Taloja, India, inaugurated (value-added services).
Shanghai office opened in China; workshop for assembly of special machines planned to open in Q3 CY26.
Execution timeline on contracts is typically two to three years; management now uses three years as the working assumption for the current book.
Headcount expansion on execution side planned, with employee cost rising.
demand_pricing: Order inflow ~INR1,200 crore in Q2, driven by demand for advanced processing, electrical steel, downstream quality and plant modernisation.
Management cited EU tariff-quota regime (18.3 million tons, 15% duty beyond quota) as supportive for hot-rolling, cold-rolling and processing-line investments.
India per capita steel consumption ~93 kg vs global ~230 kg; India steel production expected at 161.7 million tons this year.

JVD (Jet Vapor Deposition) pitched as a zinc-coating alternative to hot-dip galvanizing; customer savings cited at least INR1,000 per unit, up to 20x that, mainly for automotive and AHSS grades; first contract delayed by customer investment-approval process.
Potential cold-rolling order in the range of EUR50-100 million expected this year.
Competitors named: SMS and Danieli (Tier-1 OEMs), also Primetals; all have downstream portfolios.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore CY30 top-line target still valid, and how will it be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, as a north-star; two streams: organic (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions, which are under investigation. Volteron IP sits with John Cockerill SA, not the listed entity, and is not yet commercial.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the CY25 pro-forma revenue (~INR2,000 crore) far above reported (~INR960 crore), and can the US entity bridge the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2,000 crore was a guideline; US is not a large contributor. Revenue depends on order progress. Management expects significant H2 improvement and said the gap should not be very far if US is included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did John Cockerill SA reduce holding from ~75% to ~70.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to group priorities; SA remains a large shareholder and will get convertible preferential shares that would take it back to 72%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost structure outlook (employee cost ~INR68 crore, other expenses ~INR70 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost to rise with execution hiring; other expenses marginally below current level in next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone and consolidated order book, service revenue, and top-customer concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated ~INR4,500 crore, standalone ~INR2,200 crore. Service revenue ~one-third of Q1. Top five ~80% of revenue; standalone top are Tata Steel and JSW.

qa_highlights.question: Quantum of one-time consolidation costs in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify; said it would come back to the analyst. Costs covered transaction, forex, notional interest, legal, audit and due diligence across Belgium, Germany and China.

risks_watch: Margin pressure in Q2 from upfront costs on new projects; recovery depends on H2 execution ramp.
Revenue lumpiness: sequential decline in Q2 from Q1 project close-outs.
Consolidation and ongoing parent-company cost sharing (R&D, technical development) may persist beyond one-time items.
JVD first commercial contract repeatedly delayed by customer investment validation; Volteron not yet commercial and needs pilot validation.
Gap between INR8,000 crore CY30 target and current run-rate; acquisition plans have no detail or timeline.
Revenue guidance of ~INR2,000 crore CY25 pro-forma was not met; management did not reaffirm a specific figure.
Customer concentration: top five ~80% of revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book and long-term demand, but cautious on near-term profitability, which management called transitional. Evasive on several specifics: the consolidation-cost quantum, regional revenue split, and the reason for delays in the JVD contract and Taloja facility.
